newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas up in Q1 98 as one player buys in volume.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas up in Q1 98 as one player buys in volume.

text.p: The UK spot natural gas market saw prices rise in the winter rise yet again, as one company bought heavily in the first quarter next year.

One dealer bought six separate pieces in Q1 98, each one from a different seller. The price rose from 17.10 pence a therm to 17.20 pence over the course of the day, and was said to be well offered at 17.20 pence by the close.

The buyer pointed out that the number of trades done was a bearish indicator, as it implied that six different sellers preferred to sell gas at this price rather than holding on to it any longer, possibly expecting it to lose value.

There were also trades done in Q1 99 at similar levels to the equivalent period in 1998. A deal was confirmed done at 17.175 pence a therm, and there were also rumours that trade was done at 17.10 pence and 17.125 pence as well.
"Q1 99 is trading fairly flat to Q1 98," a trader said. "The contango seems to have evaporated. It shows there's a higher contango in the summer than in the winter."

The emphasis was on trading by quarters rather than months or other periods on Wednesday. Apart from the glut of Q1 98 trade, there were also deals reported in Q4 97, all the other quarters in 1998, and Q1 99, and there were rumours from a well-placed source that Q1 2000 traded at 17.35 pence a therm. This followed a deal in Q1 2000 late on Monday at 17.30 pence.

The prompt period was less active than recently. A company which had bought 1.4 million therms on the within day market on Tuesday and 1 million therms on Monday was back in the market on Wednesday, but only for 30,000 therms. The buyer would not speculate if that marked an end to its large buying programme.

The IPE was up in the winter, with January, February and March all trading up as 325 lots were done. Some in the market felt that the activity on the OTC market at higher prices in Q1 98 may have been partly triggered by a rise on winter futures earlier in the day.
